newsitem.title: USA: Bill offered to protect more Utah redrocks.
newsitem.headline: Bill offered to protect more Utah redrocks.

text.p: An Illinois senator on Wednesday offered legislation to designate 5.7 million acres of redrock formations in Utah as protected wilderness.
The bill, offered by Illinios Democrat Richard Durbin, would give extra protection to the portion of 22 million acres of Utah land owned by the federal Bureau of Land Management.
The bill would prohibit road-building, dams, military facilities and other construction, as well as use of motorized vehicles, in the wilderness area.
Durbin said because of "flaws in the original wilderness inventory" conducted by the BLM in the 1980s, just 3.2 million acres in southern Utah was designated as wilderness.
"As a result, the fragile, scenic lands are threatened by oil, gas and mining interests willing to sacrifice the land for short-term economic gain," he said in a statement.
Durbin said his bill had eight cosponsors so far, while a House companion bill had 105 cosponsors.
